Thank you — I’ll build a 12-week, gym-based strength program for your 30-year-old, advanced lifter at 20 weeks gestation with OB clearance for moderate strength. I’ll follow the constraints you gave: no supine after week 16, no max attempts, avoid contact sports. Because she’s an advanced lifter, we’ll keep intensity meaningful but submaximal, prioritize technique and safety, and gradually adjust volume/intensity as pregnancy progresses. The program emphasizes posterior chain, upper-body strength, single-leg work, core/postural work (pregnancy-appropriate), breathing, mobility, and recovery. Monitor for warning signs (vaginal bleeding, dizziness, chest pain, regular painful contractions, fluid leakage, decreased fetal movement, or any unusual symptoms) and stop/modify exercise if they occur.

Overview & programming principles
- Duration: 12 weeks, starting at 20 weeks gestation (so ends ~32 weeks). Split into three 4-week phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): 20–23 weeks — maintain strength, establish pregnancy-safe modifications; moderate loads RPE 6–7/10, 3 sessions/week.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): 24–27 weeks — maintain/slow progression, increase accessory and unilateral work, continue RPE 6–7, 3 sessions/week.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): 28–31/32 weeks — reduce loading slightly, increase tempo control, focus on mobility, breathing, pelvic floor prep; RPE 5–7, 3 sessions/week.
- Frequency: 3 full-body strength sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Option to add 1–2 low-impact cardio or mobility sessions (walking, swimming, stationary bike, prenatal yoga) on off days if energy allows.
- Intensity: No 1RM or maximal efforts. Use submax loads that feel challenging for prescribed reps but leave 1–3 RIR (reps in reserve). Use RPE ~6–7 first two phases, slight drop to ~5–7 in final phase.
- Exercise selection: Avoid supine presses/rows after week 16 (no flat bench lying position). Use seated/angled/standing alternatives. Avoid Valsalva — emphasize exhale during exertion and steady breathing. Avoid heavy axial compressions where discomfort arises.
- Sets/reps & progression: Primary lifts 3–4 sets of 5–8 or 6–10 depending on movement; accessory lifts 2–3 sets of 8–15. Progress by small load increases (2.5–5 lb) if RPE stays below target and form is perfect. If discomfort, regress.
- Core & pelvic floor: Avoid heavy loaded flexion or intense abdominal straining; include standing anti-extension/rotation, side-lying and hands-and-knees work, pelvic floor activation (kegels) with instruction on proper technique. Avoid traditional supine crunches and heavy loaded carries that provoke intra-abdominal pressure complaints.
- Breathing & bracing: Teach diaphragmatic breathing, avoid breath-holding and strong Valsalva. Use gentle bracing (light core engagement) rather than maximal bracing.
- Recovery & monitoring: Emphasize more sleep, hydration, snacks around sessions, and extra recovery near end of program. Reduce or stop if any concerning symptoms.

Session structure (each workout)
- Warm-up 8–12 minutes: light cardio 5 min (bike/walk), dynamic mobility for hips/shoulders/spine, activation (glute bridges variation modified to side-lying/quad/kneeling as needed), breathing and pelvic floor cues.
- Main lifts: 2–3 main compound movements per session, controlled tempo (2s concentric, 2s eccentric where comfortable), 3–4 sets.
- Accessory lifts: unilateral work, posterior chain, upper-body pulling, scapular/rotator cuff work, and pregnancy-safe core.
- Finish: gentle mobility, breathing/pelvic floor practice, and cool-down.

Detailed week-by-week plan
Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (20–23 weeks): maintain strength, establish pregnancy-safe mechanics
General guidance: RPE 6–7. Avoid supine. Use seated/standing bench press alternatives (incline or seated dumbbell/landmine). Keep progress conservative.

Week 1 (Baseline week; establish loads)
Session A (Lower bias)
- Warm-up 8–10 min.
- Goblet or front squat (front rack or goblet; use DB/KB): 4 x 6 (2–3 RIR). If balance or belly restricts, use safety-bar or high-bar with caution.
- Romanian deadlift (barbell or dumbbells): 3 x 8. Hinge emphasis, moderate weight.
- Split squat (rear foot elevated or stationary Bulgarian): 3 x 8 each leg (use DBs).
- Glute bridge (single-leg supported or double — if supine uncomfortable, use hip thrust on incline bench set to upright/modify to standing banded hip hinge): 3 x 10. If supine is uncomfortable, do banded standing hip extension or quadruped hip extension.
- Calf raises (single or double): 3 x 12.
- Core & pelvic floor: Side-lying plank (knees bent) 3 x 20–30s each side; pelvic floor activation 3 x 8 gentle holds.

Session B (Upper bias)
- Warm-up.
- Seated DB incline press (or landmine press): 4 x 6–8.
- Seated cable row or chest-supported row (avoid supine): 4 x 8.
- One-arm DB row (bench-supported, not supine): 3 x 8 each.
- Lateral raises: 3 x 12.
- Face pulls (band or cable) for scapular health: 3 x 15.
- Biceps curl: 2 x 12.
- Triceps pushdown or overhead triceps extension (seated): 2 x 12.
- Core: Bird-dog (hands-and-knees) 3 x 8 each side with breathing.

Session C (Full-body/Posterior bias)
- Warm-up.
- Trap-bar deadlift or hex-bar DL (safer for pelvis/center of mass): 4 x 5–6.
- Bulgarian split squat (dumbbells): 3 x 8 each.
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift (DB): 3 x 8 each.
- Reverse lunge (walking or in-place): 3 x 8 each.
- Cable pull-through or banded good morning: 3 x 12.
- Upper back: Seated high-rep rows or supported rear-delt work: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Seated Pallof press (cable or band) 3 x 10 each side.

- Add 2.5–5 lb to main lifts if RPE lower than target and no symptoms.
- Slightly increase accessory reps (toward upper end) or sets if feeling strong.
- Continue pelvic floor and breathing daily short sessions (1–2 minutes multiple times per day).

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (24–27 weeks): maintain strength while increasing unilateral work and control
General guidance: RPE 6–7. Continue to avoid supine and heavy Valsalva. Increase emphasis on balance and single-leg strength and upper back/postural muscles.

Short answer: No — she should not test a true 1RM at week 12 (or at any point during pregnancy).

Why not
- Maximal one-rep attempts increase intra-abdominal and intrathoracic pressure (Valsalva), which raises blood pressure and cardiac strain. During pregnancy this can reduce placental blood flow transiently and increase maternal cardiovascular stress.
- 1RM testing often pushes to failure and requires breath-holding or maximal bracing patterns that we intentionally avoid in pregnancy.
- Maximal loads also increase risk of musculoskeletal injury, pelvic floor overload, and abrupt fatigue or dizziness — all undesirable when pregnant.
- Clinical guidance and your OB clearance (which permitted moderate strength, with no max attempts) explicitly contraindicate maximal testing.

What she can do instead (safe, satisfying alternatives that still allow strength feedback)
- Submaximal testing with estimated 1RM from higher-rep sets
  - Example: perform a well-rested set of 3–5 reps at a challenging but safe load (stop with 1–2 RIR). Use validated prediction formulas to estimate 1RM. This gives an objective number without maximal effort.
- Heavy-but-submax protocol (allowed at RPE up to ~8 occasionally)
  - Use singles/doubles at a heavy but submaximal load in cluster format: e.g., 4 sets of 2 reps with 20–30s intra-cluster rest, stopping each set with 1–2 RIR. This provides a strong training stimulus and performance feedback without an all-out attempt.
- 3RM or 5RM testing (submaximal criteria)
  - Test a true 3RM or 5RM rather than 1RM, but only if cleared and stopping with 1 RIR is ensured. Use careful breathing cues and longer rests. Prefer 5RM for safety.
- Velocity- or RPE-based assessment
  - If you have a velocity device, monitor bar speed at submax loads to infer neuromuscular readiness. Or, use consistent RPE targets across weeks to track relative strength and fatigue.
- Performance benchmarks not requiring maximal load
  - Track number of reps performed at a fixed submax load (e.g., reps at 70% pre-pregnancy working weight), or carry distances/weights (farmer carry), Pallof band level, or timed holds (side plank), which reflect strength and work capacity.

If you still want a definitive “peak” testing session at week 12, do this instead
- Protocol: Submax 3–5RM testing session (NOT 1RM), executed only if she feels well that day and after OB confirmation. Use seated/landmine/safety-bar/trap-bar variations (not flat bench). Steps:
  1. Full warm-up and breathing/pelvic-floor prep.
  2. Work up to a heavy 3–5RM set using gradual increments, never going to technical failure; stop with 1 RIR.
  3. Prefer 3–5RM on trap-bar deadlift, safety-bar squat, seated DB press, or single-arm landmine press — movements that avoid supine and reduce anterior compression.
  4. Use long rests (2.5–3.5 min) between warm-up and heavy sets; avoid breath-holding — cue exhale on exertion and light pelvic-floor lift.
  5. Record load and RPE; estimate 1RM with an accepted formula if desired.
  6. Keep total volume low — limit to 1–2 tested lifts that day and finish the session.

Safety checks and red flags during testing
- Stop immediately if any: dizziness, lightheadedness, shortness of breath beyond normal, palpitations, vaginal bleeding, uterine contractions, pelvic pressure/heaviness, or any acute pain.
- Monitor fetal movement per her OB’s advice.
- Ensure hydration and carbohydrate availability before testing.

Recommendation
- Strongly prefer submax testing (3–5RM or estimated 1RM from a 3–5RM or 5–8RM) and cluster-set heavy singles with 1–2 RIR rather than an actual 1RM. This meets her desire to “feel like she’s training hard” while staying within safe pregnancy practice.

- Bird-dog with 3s hold: 3 x 8 each.
- Standing cable anti-extension holds: 3 x 10s x 4.
- Single-leg RDL into core stabilization: 3 x 6 each.

- Single-arm landmine press (half-kneeling): 4 x 6 each.
- Suitcase carry / single-arm farmer carry: 3 x 30–45s each side.
- Tall-kneeling cable chop (controlled): 3 x 8 each.
- Side-lying clams + side plank: 3 x 10 clams, 3 x 25–35s plank.

Core C — Dynamic posterior chain & stability
- Single-leg RDL into cable row: 3 x 6–8 each side.
- Banded pull-throughs with isometric torso hold: 3 x 10.
- Seated band-resisted trunk rotation: 3 x 10 each side.
- Modified (incline) dead-bug: 3 x 8 each.

- Monday: Strength A (moderate lower)
- Tuesday: Cardio (low volume, pool or recumbent)
- Wednesday: Strength B (upper moderate — pressing)
- Thursday: Mobility / swim / light active recovery
- Friday: Strength C (full-body/unilateral moderate)
- Saturday: Cardio or long walk (easy)
- Sunday: Rest

Session A — Monday (Lower & control)
- Goblet/front squat (lighter than Phase 2): 3 x 6–8.
- Trap-bar deadlift or rack pull (mid-shin): 3 x 5–6 moderate.
- Split squat or step-ups: 3 x 8 each.
- Hamstring curl or RDL: 3 x 8–12 (lighter).
- Core: Standing Pallof press 3 x 10 each.

Session B — Wednesday (Upper moderate — press)
- Seated incline DB press or seated DB press: 3 x 6–8.
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10.
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10.
- Landmine single-arm press: 3 x 8 each.
- Face pulls + lateral raises superset: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Quadruped bird-dog 3 x 8 each.

Session C — Friday (Posterior/unilateral)
- Single-leg RDL or kettlebell deadlift: 3 x 6–8 each.
- Step-ups or static split squat: 3 x 8 each.
- Banded glute bridges (standing or incline): 3 x 12.
- Farmer carry light/moderate: 2 x 45–60s.
- Core: Side plank 3 x 30s.

Cardio (Phase 3)
- Tuesday: 25–30 min pool swim or recumbent bike, RPE 3–5.
- Saturday: 20–30 min brisk walk (flat) or easy swim.
- Optional short interval session (only if energy allows): 5 x 60–90s at RPE 6 with 2–3 min recovery — keep total session short.

  Option A — 3RM submax test (only if she feels excellent and with OB approval)
    - Warm-up thoroughly and practice pelvic-floor breathing.
    - Choose 1–2 lifts that avoid supine: trap-bar deadlift, safety-bar/front squat, seated DB press, or single-arm landmine press.
    - Work up to a heavy 3RM set but stop with 1 RIR — do not go to absolute failure.
    - Use long rests (3–4 min) and limit total tested lifts to 1–2.
    - Record loads and RPE. Estimate 1RM if you wish via formula but do not attempt it.
  Option B — Heavy cluster singles (submax feedback)
    - Example: Trap-bar 4 sets x (3 clusters of 2 reps) with 15–20s intra-cluster rest at a heavy but submax weight (stop with ~1–2 RIR).
    - Seated DB press: 4 sets x 3 reps cluster style.
  Option C — Volume benchmark
    - Reps to technical failure are not allowed; instead pick a fixed submax load (e.g., 70% of pre-pregnancy working load) and perform AMRAP while stopping 2 reps before failure — track reps to compare week-to-week.
  Option D — Performance & stability tests
    - Pallof band level, farmer carry weight/distance, side-plank hold time, or carry distance at fixed weight. These provide objective feedback without maximal loading.

- Monday: Light lower session (3 x 5 moderate)
- Tuesday: Active recovery / pelvic-floor breathing
- Wednesday (testing day): Warm-up thoroughly → perform selected conservative 3RM or cluster test on 1–2 lifts only → finish with light mobility and breathing practice → stop immediately on any symptoms.
- Thursday: Rest or mobility
- Friday: Light upper session (low volume)
- Saturday: Easy walk/pool
- Sunday: Rest

Core (Phase 3)
- 2–3 sessions/week: Pallof presses, tall-kneeling landmine presses, bird-dogs, side-planks; daily pelvic-floor breathing & holds with emphasis on endurance holds (3 x 8–12s comfortable).

- Weeks 5–8: Intensified Phase 2. Strength M/W/F heavier + clusters. Cardio Tue (intervals) & Sat (steady). Core 3–4x/week.
- Weeks 9–11: Taper/maintain. Strength M/W/F moderate. Cardio Tue/Sat low-volume. Core 2–3x/week + daily pelvic-floor.  
- Week 12: Conservative testing alternatives; avoid 1RM. Maintain safety and reduce overall volume.

- Calorie: add ~+250–350 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance during 2nd trimester; adjust by weight gain trajectory and appetite. Example: maintenance estimate = bodyweight(kg) x 30–35 kcal; add 250–350 kcal. Adjust per OB/Dietitian and monitor weekly weight.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (aim 1.4 g/kg as a practical target). Distribute 20–40 g protein per meal/snack.
- Fat: ~25–35% of calories, prioritize mono & polyunsaturated fats; ensure DHA intake (~200–300 mg/day) via supplement or fatty fish (low-mercury).
- Carbs: remainder of calories, prioritized around workouts.
- Hydration: ≥2.3 L/day baseline; more with exercise/heat.
- Meal timing: pre-workout snack 30–60 min prior (carb + protein), post-workout protein + carbs within 1–2 hours.
- Supplements: prenatal multivitamin with folate; iron only if indicated; vitamin D per OB; omega-3 DHA per OB; protein powder safe (pasteurised whey or plant-based).

- Diaphragmatic breathing: 5–10 slow breaths pre/post sessions.
- Pelvic-floor quicks: 10 quick contractions daily.
- Pelvic-floor endurance holds: 3 x 5–12s depending on comfort and stage (increase hold time gradually).
- Integrate light pelvic-floor cueing during lifts (light lift on initiation).

- No flat bench press: use seated incline DB press, seated machine press, landmine, or Smith seated incline.
- No supine hip thrusts unless incline bench is used and comfortable — prefer standing banded hip extensions or incline-supported thrusts with torso elevated.
- If pelvic pressure, leakage, or pain occurs: reduce load/volume, switch to aquatic or recumbent cardio, avoid heavy carries, and refer to pelvic-floor PT.

- Stop training and contact OB for vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, chest pain, dizziness/faintness, regular painful contractions, decreased fetal movement, or sudden severe calf swelling/shortness of breath.
- Track RPE and symptoms in each session. If baseline RPE for same workload rises, reduce load or volume.

- Use pre-pregnancy 3–5RM numbers to estimate safe working loads: target ~70–85% of pre-pregnancy working loads for Phase 2 heavy days but always on perceived exertion (1–2 RIR). Start conservative and adjust upward only if RPE and symptoms allow.
- Example: If pre-preg DB press 5RM = 30 kg, Phase 2 heavy seated DB press sets might start ~22–26 kg with progression of 1–2.5 kg increments as tolerated.
- Track RPE: if RPE > 8 on multiple sets or symptoms occur, regress.

- Keep close communication with her OB and refer to a pelvic-floor physiotherapist if any leakage or pelvic pain occurs.
- Avoid maximal 1RM testing at any point. Use the Week-12 conservative submax testing options instead.
- Encourage sleep, hydration, and gentle mobility; re-assess weekly and adjust loads and volume based on symptoms and energy.

Below is a complete 12‑week gym-based strength, cardio, pressing, core, and nutrition program for your prenatal client. It starts at 20 weeks gestation and runs through ~32 weeks. It incorporates all your constraints (OB cleared for moderate strength; no supine after week 16; no maximal attempts; avoid contact sports) and the adjustments you requested: intensified Phase 2, safe bench-press alternatives (bench-feel pressing), added cardio, and a progressive pregnancy-safe core plan. I’ve also included the nutrition plan you requested earlier and a safe “peak” testing alternative for Week 12. Use the program as a template and adjust loads based on her RPE, symptom feedback, and comfort.

How to use this program — essentials
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri), 2 cardio sessions/week (Tue/Sat), 1 mobility/active recovery day (Thu) and 1 rest day (Sun). You can swap days to fit her schedule.
- Intensity guidance:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): RPE ~6–7, stop sets with 1–3 RIR.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8; intensified): RPE ~6–8 on main work; some sets may reach RPE 7–8 but stop with 1–2 RIR. Use clusters/rest-pause for intensity rather than 1RM testing.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): taper slightly; RPE ~5–7. Week 12 includes a conservative submax testing protocol (3RM or heavy cluster work) — no true 1RM.
- No supine after week 16 — all pressing and hip-thrust alternatives follow this rule.
- Breathing & pelvic floor: avoid Valsalva. Teach diaphragmatic breathing and light pelvic-floor engagement (lift) on exertion. Daily pelvic-floor practice recommended.
- Progressions: increase load by 2.5–5 lb only if RPE allows and no symptoms. Increase band tension, carry weight/distance, or add sets/time for core where appropriate.
- Stop and contact OB if any red flags: vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, regular painful contractions, dizziness/fainting, chest pain, shortness of breath beyond normal, sudden calf swelling, decreased fetal movement, or any acute severe pain.

Overview — Phases
- Phase 1 Weeks 1–4 (20–23 weeks): maintain strength, technique, pregnancy-safe mechanics. Strength 3x/wk; cardio 2x/wk; core integrated 3–5x/wk.
- Phase 2 Weeks 5–8 (24–27 weeks): intensified; heavier but submax work, cluster sets, more unilateral, pressing frequency increased. Strength 3x/wk; cardio 2x/wk (one controlled interval); core 3–4x/wk.
- Phase 3 Weeks 9–12 (28–31/32 weeks): maintain with slight taper; more tempo and control, pelvic-floor/labor prep; Week 12 has conservative submax testing option (3RM/cluster). Strength 3x/wk; cardio 2x/wk (lower volume); core 2–3x/wk + daily pelvic-floor work.

Daily warm-up (8–12 min) — perform before every strength session
- 5 min light cardio (bike/walk/elliptical)
- Dynamic mobility: thoracic rotations, shoulder dislocations with band, hip CARs or leg swings
- Activation: banded lateral walks (1 x 20 steps), glute bridges or standing banded hip hinge (2 x 10) — perform standing variants if supine uncomfortable
- Brief breathing & pelvic-floor cue: 3 diaphragmatic breaths + 1 set of 5 pelvic-floor quicks

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4 (20–23 weeks) — moderate, technique-focused
Goal: maintain strength; set baseline loads and technique; press work introduced seated/incline; core foundation.

Weekly layout (example)
- Monday: Strength A (Lower bias) + short core
- Tuesday: Cardio (steady-state) + pelvic-floor breathing
- Wednesday: Strength B (Upper bias, pressing) + short core
- Thursday: Mobility / light cardio / swim
- Friday: Strength C (Full-body/posterior bias) + short core
- Saturday: Cardio (pool or easy walk)
- Sunday: Rest

Week 1 (establish loads) — repeat for Weeks 2–4 with small progressions
Session A — Lower bias (Mon)
- Front squat or goblet squat: 4 x 6 (RPE 6–7). Use safety-bar if available.
- Romanian deadlift (barbell or DB): 3 x 8.
- Bulgarian split squat (DB): 3 x 8 each leg.
- Standing banded glute extension or incline hip thrust (incline bench if comfortable): 3 x 10.
- Calf raises: 3 x 12.
- Core finish (after weights): Side-lying plank (knees bent) 3 x 20–30s per side; pelvic-floor quicks 3 x 10.

Session B — Upper bias (Wed)
- Seated incline dumbbell press (or seated DB press): 4 x 6–8.
- Seated cable row or chest-supported row: 4 x 8.
- One-arm DB row (bench-supported): 3 x 8 each.
- Lateral raises: 3 x 12.
- Face pulls: 3 x 15.
- Triceps pushdown (seated/standing): 2 x 12.
- Core: Bird-dog 3 x 8 each side.

Session C — Full-body/posterior (Fri)
- Trap-bar deadlift: 4 x 5–6.
- Reverse lunge: 3 x 8 each.
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 8 each.
- Cable pull-through or banded good morning: 3 x 12.
- Seated/standing row high-rep for upper back: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Seated Pallof press 3 x 10 each side.

Cardio (Tues & Sat)
- Tuesday: 25–35 min steady-state stationary bike or brisk walk (RPE 4–5).
- Saturday: 20–30 min pool swim or easy elliptic (low impact).

Core (integrated daily mini-sessions)
- Daily breathing + pelvic-floor quicks: 5–10 breaths, 10 quicks, 3 holds x 5–8s.
- Core workouts after strength sessions (as listed).

Progression for Phase 1
- Add 2.5–5 lb to main lifts if RPE <=6 and technique fine. Increase accessory reps to top of range before adding load.

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8 (24–27 weeks) — intensified (she wants to feel like she’s training)
Goal: heavier submaximal loads, cluster techniques, more pressing frequency, heavier core work without supine.

Weekly layout (example)
- Monday: Strength A (Lower heavy)
- Tuesday: Cardio intervals (controlled)
- Wednesday: Strength B (Upper heavy — pressing focus)
- Thursday: Active recovery / mobility / swim
- Friday: Strength C (Posterior & unilateral heavy)
- Saturday: Cardio steady-state (pool/walk)
- Sunday: Rest

Key intensity rules for Phase 2
- Main lifts: 3–6 reps, 3–5 sets, target RPE 7–8 on some working sets, stop with 1–2 RIR.
- Use cluster sets where appropriate: e.g., 4 sets of 6 as 3 clusters of 2 reps with 15–20s intra-cluster rest.
- Two pressing sessions/week: one heavy (strength-ish), one volume (hypertrophy-style).
- Daily pelvic-floor breathing practice and 3–4 core sessions per week (~12–18 min).

Weeks 5 & 6 — progressive template (repeat weeks 5–8 with small increases in load or intensity)
Week 5 — sample

Session A — Lower heavy (Mon)
- Trap-bar deadlift: 5 x 3 (heavy but stop with 1–2 RIR). Rest 2.5–3 min.
- Safety-bar or front squat: 4 x 4–6. Rest 2–3 min.
- Bulgarian split squat (heavy DB): 3 x 6–8 each leg.
- Romanian deadlift (moderate-heavy): 3 x 6–8.
- Standing banded hip extension: 3 x 10.
- Core: Pallof press (tall kneeling or standing) 3 x 8 each.

Session B — Cardio intervals (Tue)
- Warm-up 8–10 min walk or bike.
- 5 x 90–120s at RPE 6–7 (bike or incline walk) with 2–3 min easy recovery.
- Cool-down 5–10 min.

Session C — Upper heavy (Wed) — pressing focus
- Warm-up: band dislocations, light DB press 2 x 10.
- Seated single-arm DB press: 5 x 4–5 each arm (push to RPE 7–8 final sets).
- Landmine press (double or single-arm): 4 x 6–8.
- Chest-supported row: 4 x 6–8.
- Weighted lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 4 x 6–8.
- Face pulls & lateral raise superset: 3 x 12–15 each.
- Triceps heavy: close-grip cable or seated triceps extension 3 x 8–10.
- Core: Quadruped dead-bug 3 x 8 each.

Session D — Mobility (Thu)
- 20–30 min swim, prenatal yoga, or mobility routine.

Session E — Posterior & unilateral heavy (Fri)
- RDL (barbell or DB): 4 x 5–6 (focus on eccentric).
- Heavy step-ups (DB): 4 x 5–6 each leg.
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 6 each.
- Glute-ham or machine hamstring curl: 3 x 6–8.
- Farmer carries (moderate-heavy, controlled) 3 x 40–60 m (avoid breath-holding).
- Core: Side plank variations 3 x 20–30s.

Session F — Cardio steady (Sat)
- 25–35 min pool swim or easy recumbent bike walk, RPE 3–5.

Weeks 6–8 progression/tactics
- Week 6: introduce one cluster set on trap-bar or seated DB press (e.g., 4 x [3 clusters of 2]) for a heavier feel without a 1RM.
- Week 7: increase DB press loads by 2.5–5 lb if RPE manageable; increase Pallof band tension.
- Week 8: peak intensity week of Phase 2 — allow a couple of sets at RPE 7–8; reduce accessory volume slightly if fatigue occurs.

Core (Phase 2 — 3–4x/week, 12–18 min sessions)
Rotate A/B/C templates across the week:

Core A — Anti-extension & loaded core
- Half-kneeling or standing Pallof press: 4 x 8 each side (heavier band).
- Bird-dog with 3s hold: 3 x 8 each.
- Standing cable anti-extension holds: 3 x 10s x 4.
- Single-leg RDL into core stabilization: 3 x 6 each.

Core B — Anti-rotation & carries
- Single-arm landmine press (half-kneeling): 4 x 6 each.
- Suitcase carry / single-arm farmer carry: 3 x 30–45s each side.
- Tall-kneeling cable chop (controlled): 3 x 8 each.
- Side-lying clams + side plank: 3 x 10 clams, 3 x 25–35s plank.

Core C — Dynamic posterior chain & stability
- Single-leg RDL into cable row: 3 x 6–8 each side.
- Banded pull-throughs with isometric torso hold: 3 x 10.
- Seated band-resisted trunk rotation: 3 x 10 each side.
- Modified (incline) dead-bug: 3 x 8 each.

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12 (28–31/32 weeks) — maintenance, taper, labor prep
Goal: maintain strength and stability with reduced absolute loads and more focus on breathing, pelvic-floor endurance, and comfort. Week 12 contains conservative submax testing alternatives (NO 1RM).

Weekly layout (example)
- Monday: Strength A (moderate lower)
- Tuesday: Cardio (low volume, pool or recumbent)
- Wednesday: Strength B (upper moderate — pressing)
- Thursday: Mobility / swim / light active recovery
- Friday: Strength C (full-body/unilateral moderate)
- Saturday: Cardio or long walk (easy)
- Sunday: Rest

Weeks 9–11 — sample sessions

Session A — Monday (Lower & control)
- Goblet/front squat (lighter than Phase 2): 3 x 6–8.
- Trap-bar deadlift or rack pull (mid-shin): 3 x 5–6 moderate.
- Split squat or step-ups: 3 x 8 each.
- Hamstring curl or RDL: 3 x 8–12 (lighter).
- Core: Standing Pallof press 3 x 10 each.

Session B — Wednesday (Upper moderate — press)
- Seated incline DB press or seated DB press: 3 x 6–8.
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10.
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10.
- Landmine single-arm press: 3 x 8 each.
- Face pulls + lateral raises superset: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Quadruped bird-dog 3 x 8 each.

Session C — Friday (Posterior/unilateral)
- Single-leg RDL or kettlebell deadlift: 3 x 6–8 each.
- Step-ups or static split squat: 3 x 8 each.
- Banded glute bridges (standing or incline): 3 x 12.
- Farmer carry light/moderate: 2 x 45–60s.
- Core: Side plank 3 x 30s.

Cardio (Phase 3)
- Tuesday: 25–30 min pool swim or recumbent bike, RPE 3–5.
- Saturday: 20–30 min brisk walk (flat) or easy swim.
- Optional short interval session (only if energy allows): 5 x 60–90s at RPE 6 with 2–3 min recovery — keep total session short.

Week 12 — conservative “peak” & testing alternatives (NO 1RM)
- DO NOT test true 1RM. If she wants a performance test, use one or two of these safe options (choose max two lifts for that day):
  Option A — 3RM submax test (only if she feels excellent and with OB approval)
    - Warm-up thoroughly and practice pelvic-floor breathing.
    - Choose 1–2 lifts that avoid supine: trap-bar deadlift, safety-bar/front squat, seated DB press, or single-arm landmine press.
    - Work up to a heavy 3RM set but stop with 1 RIR — do not go to absolute failure.
    - Use long rests (3–4 min) and limit total tested lifts to 1–2.
    - Record loads and RPE. Estimate 1RM if you wish via formula but do not attempt it.
  Option B — Heavy cluster singles (submax feedback)
    - Example: Trap-bar 4 sets x (3 clusters of 2 reps) with 15–20s intra-cluster rest at a heavy but submax weight (stop with ~1–2 RIR).
    - Seated DB press: 4 sets x 3 reps cluster style.
  Option C — Volume benchmark
    - Reps to technical failure are not allowed; instead pick a fixed submax load (e.g., 70% of pre-pregnancy working load) and perform AMRAP while stopping 2 reps before failure — track reps to compare week-to-week.
  Option D — Performance & stability tests
    - Pallof band level, farmer carry weight/distance, side-plank hold time, or carry distance at fixed weight. These provide objective feedback without maximal loading.

Week 12 sample schedule (if testing)
- Monday: Light lower session (3 x 5 moderate)
- Tuesday: Active recovery / pelvic-floor breathing
- Wednesday (testing day): Warm-up thoroughly → perform selected conservative 3RM or cluster test on 1–2 lifts only → finish with light mobility and breathing practice → stop immediately on any symptoms.
- Thursday: Rest or mobility
- Friday: Light upper session (low volume)
- Saturday: Easy walk/pool
- Sunday: Rest

Core (Phase 3)
- 2–3 sessions/week: Pallof presses, tall-kneeling landmine presses, bird-dogs, side-planks; daily pelvic-floor breathing & holds with emphasis on endurance holds (3 x 8–12s comfortable).

Full 12-week microcycle summary (by week)
- Weeks 1–4: Foundation (moderate loads). Strength M/W/F. Cardio Tue/Sat. Core mini-sessions daily with 3x/week focused after lifting.
- Weeks 5–8: Intensified Phase 2. Strength M/W/F heavier + clusters. Cardio Tue (intervals) & Sat (steady). Core 3–4x/week.
- Weeks 9–11: Taper/maintain. Strength M/W/F moderate. Cardio Tue/Sat low-volume. Core 2–3x/week + daily pelvic-floor.  
- Week 12: Conservative testing alternatives; avoid 1RM. Maintain safety and reduce overall volume.
